A mobile platform (e.g., a UAV-borne SDF system) could augment the scanning and, during the reconstruction phase, could fuse X- radiographs with LBNL Report #2001653 radiation data collected onboard the SDF system. The radiographs would constrain attenuation information. The concept of a co-located basckscatter radiography and SDF sensor system is a sophisticated solution that could provide better context for where within a cargo container an anomaly was observed. Small SDF platforms could be used to investigate inside a container, once opened, but the primary attraction of SDF lies in being able to perform the inspection from afar (for safety), whether autonomously or via radio control. A second possible use of SDF is the examination of containers in shipping yards or on ships at a portorwhileapproachingit. Intheshipyardcase,SDFplatformscouldperformregularsweepsover and around container stacks, imaging and searching for radiation sources. When ships are moving, the SDF mapping logic needs to be able to compensate for that motion. SLAM solutions should be capable of doing so, but it has not been tested within the context of SDF applications. Also note that SDF platforms have already been used to image stacks of shipping containers containing radiological sources [22]. Imaging fidelity and autonomy would be important to mature for such uses. Similarly, a mobile SDF platform could be used to “pre-scan” trucks at a border crossing, movingsuspiciousonesdirectlyintosecondaryinspectionorunofficialcrossingscouldbemonitored using UAV-based SDF systems. A similar but non-radiological, use of an SDF-capable system in border security would be in performing close inspections of specific locations for buried targets e.g., tunnels, but the search would have to be triggered and targeted via other measurement modalities. Combining lidar (to map the terrestrial environment/geometry) with those other measurement modalities could help position the buried target relative to visible over-ground structures for better interpretation of the fused images. Most NSDD applications would require significant enhancements in the endurance of the robotic systems that would carry the SDF payload. Potentially, adding new sensors (e.g., ground penetrating sensors) and the incorporation of radiographs e.g., backscatter X-ray images as priors for shielding in the reconstruction of the contents of shipping containers would be technologically attractive. These new sensors would require their own specific reconstruction techniques to be implemented inside the current suite. 5 SDF R&D Needs The discussion in Sec. 4 shows the wide range of applications that SDF could be adapted to, as well as the enhancements necessary to do so. However, they contain some common themes: • The mobility of the SDF platform makes it of tremendous use, as it allows imaging from multiple directions and therefore enables circumventing of shielding effects, mitigation of 1/r2 distance effects, and localization through triangulation and/or imaging. • Awidevarietyofsensortypeswouldbenefitdifferentapplications,buttheyarenotallrequired together; rather, one chooses a handful of sensors to mount on a platform.
